Head_and_Face: Head is triangular with a pointed snout.
Eyes are large, independently mobile, covered by a transparent spectacle (fixed eyelid).
Males exhibit a pink or red dewlap (throat fan).
Body_and_Plumage: Body is slender.
Coloration ranges from bright green to brown depending on mood, temperature, and social context.
Skin is smooth with fine granular scales.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Adhesive toe pads on all five digits of each foot; toes are arranged in opposing groups (zygodactyl) creating a pincer-like grip.
Tail is prehensile, capable of coiling around branches.
Dorsal crest is absent.

Head_and_Face: Head is elongated and pointed with large, alert eyes.
Tongue is forked, used for chemoreception.
Body_and_Plumage: Body is streamlined and laterally compressed.
Coloration varies: common patterns include longitudinal stripes (yellow, white, or blue on dark brown or green background), spotted patterns, or uniform coloration.
Scales are small, smooth, and overlapping creating a sleek, reflective surface.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Limbs are long and slender with five clawed digits; digits are elongated.
Tail is cylindrical, laterally compressed at the base, and extremely long (two-thirds or more of total body length) with a pointed tip.

Head_and_Face: Head is large and triangular with a prominent nuchal crest (row of enlarged scales) at the back of the head.
Eyes are large and prominent with round pupils.
Body_and_Plumage: Body is robust.
Males exhibit vivid breeding coloration: bright blue head and shoulders with orange or red body and tail.
Females and non-breeding males are dull brown or grey.
Skin is covered in small, keeled (ridged) scales creating a rough, textured appearance.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Limbs are moderately long with five clawed digits; digits are slender.
Tail is long and laterally compressed, longer than body length.
Dorsal crest of spiny scales runs from the nape along the back.

Head_and_Face: Head is elongated with large eyes and a pointed snout.
Body_and_Plumage: Body is slender.
Most distinctive feature is the expansive neck frill: a large, circular ruff of skin normally folded flat but can be rapidly expanded into a wide, umbrella-like display.
Frill interior is brightly colored (orange, red, or yellow) with dark margins.
Body coloration is grey-brown to olive with darker mottling.
Skin is covered in small, keeled scales with a rough texture.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Limbs are long and slender with five clawed digits adapted for climbing.
Tail is extremely long (two-thirds of total length) and laterally compressed.
Dorsal crest of small spines runs from the nape along the back.

Head_and_Face: Head is elongated and flattened with large eyes and a pointed snout.
Body_and_Plumage: Body is elongated with short limbs, creating a snake-like appearance.
Lateral fold of loose, granular skin running along each side of the body from the neck to the vent.
Dorsal scales are large, rectangular, and keeled arranged in regular transverse rows creating a cross-hatched texture.
Coloration is brown to grey with darker crossbands or uniform.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Limbs are short but well-developed with five clawed digits.
Tail is long, laterally compressed, and capable of autotomy; regenerated tail is shorter and smoother.

Head_and_Face: Head is broad and blunt with small eyes and a forked tongue.
Body_and_Plumage: Body is robust, heavy-bodied and cylindrical.
Vivid black with irregular pink, orange, or yellow bands and spots covering the entire dorsal surface.
Skin is covered in small, bead-like osteoderms (bony deposits) embedded in the scales, creating a rough, granular texture.
Tail comprises approximately one-third of total length, used for fat storage.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Limbs are short and stout with five clawed digits; digits are robust and adapted for digging.

Head_and_Face: Head is elongated and pointed with large, prominent eyes and a pointed snout.
Body_and_Plumage: Body is slender.
Males exhibit vivid emerald-green dorsal coloration during breeding season with a bright blue throat and belly.
Females and juveniles are brown or olive-green with darker longitudinal stripes or uniform coloration.
Skin is covered in small, smooth, glossy scales creating a sleek, reflective surface.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Limbs are moderately long with five clawed digits; digits are slender.
Tail is extremely long (two-thirds of total length), cylindrical, and easily autotomized; regenerated tail is shorter and duller.

Head_and_Face: Head is crowned with a prominent casque (helmet-like crest) composed of raised scales forming a conical or pyramidal structure.
Eyes are large, conical, and independently mobile, each covered by a transparent spectacle with a small aperture for the pupil.
Body_and_Plumage: Body is laterally compressed with a high, arched back.
Skin coloration is highly variable, ranging from green to brown to yellow with patterned bands, spots, or stripes.
Color change is rapid and controlled by specialized chromatophores.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Prehensile tail coils tightly into a spiral when not in use.
Feet are zygodactyl (toes fused into opposing bundles) creating a pincer-like grip.
Tongue is extremely long (exceeding body length) and projectile.

Head_and_Face: Head is large, broad, and flattened with a blunt snout.
Mouth contains 60 serrated, recurved teeth up to 2.5 cm in length.
Eyes are small and dark with yellow irises.
Forked tongue is yellow and constantly flicking.
Body_and_Plumage: Body is massive and robust.
Coloration is uniform grey-brown to dark brown with a rough, armored appearance.
Scales are non-overlapping and tuberculate (warty) creating a rugged, dinosaur-like texture.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Limbs are massive and columnar with five curved, clawed digits; claws are thick, laterally compressed, and up to 10 cm in length.
Tail is long, muscular, and laterally compressed, used as a weapon in combat.

Head_and_Face: Head is broad and triangular with a V-shaped snout (narrower than alligator).
Jaws are massive with 64-72 conical, interlocking teeth visible when mouth is closed.
Eyes are positioned dorsally on the head with vertical slit pupils and a nictitating membrane.
Nostrils are positioned at the tip of the snout.
Body_and_Plumage: Body is elongated and heavily armored.
Body is covered in thick, bony scutes (osteoderms) arranged in regular longitudinal rows along the dorsal surface.
Scutes are dark brown to grey with a rough, heavily textured appearance.
Ventral surface is covered in smooth, rectangular scales that are pale yellow to white.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Limbs are short and stout with webbed feet; forelimbs have five digits, hind limbs have four.
Tail is laterally compressed and muscular, comprising half of total body length.
